newsitem.title: GERMANY: Austrian Airlines hopes for 97 div - paper.
newsitem.headline: Austrian Airlines hopes for 97 div - paper.

text.p: Austrian Airlines aims to pay a dividend for the calendar year 1997, the first dividend paid to shareholders since 1991, a German newspaper will report on Thursday.

The Handelsblatt daily quoted Austrian Airlines chief executives Herbert Bammer and Mario Rehulka saying the chief goal of the airline for the current year is to resume a dividend payout to shareholders for 1997.
"The primary corporate goal of Bammer and Rehuulka is to pay a dividend again for 1997," the newspaper said in an advance text of the article to appear in Thursday editions.
Bammer told Reuters earlier on Wednesday that the airline does not plan to pay a dividend for 1996 despite a rise in parent pre-tax earnings and a narrower operating loss.
In the Handelsblatt article, the two executives said the airline was on track to post a pre-tax profit in 1997 of 300 million schillings.

They said the airline aimed to cut operating costs to 19 percent of turnover from the current level of 23 percent. They said they wanted to follow Lufthansa's model and cut commissions to travel agencies.
